blocks.readview: We study the problem of sampling from the probability measure \mu(\mathrm{d}x)=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}\,\mathrm{d}x on \mathbb{R}^{d} , where V\in C^{2}(\mathbb{R}^{d}) satisfies, for 0<\alpha\leq\beta ,
\alpha I\preceq\nabla^{2}V(x)\preceq\beta I\,,\hskip 20.00003ptx\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\kappa\coloneqq\tfrac{\beta}{\alpha}\,. (1.1)
The main result of this paper is the following.
Our algorithm operates on the augmented distribution underlying the proximal sampler of Lee, Shen, and Tian [ 17 ] . For a scale \eta\in(0,1/\beta] , consider the joint law
\pi_{\eta}(\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y)\propto\exp\Bigl\{-V(x)-\frac{\|x-y\|^{2}}{2\eta}\Bigr\}\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}y\,. (2.6)
The original proximal sampler algorithm performs Gibbs sampling on \pi_{\eta} . Namely, under \pi_{\eta} one may generate the joint state as
X\sim\mu\,,\hskip 20.00003ptZ\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I)\ \text{independently}\,,\hskip 20.00003ptY=X+\sqrt{\eta}\,Z\,. (2.7)

Its X -marginal is \pi_{\eta}^{X}=\mu . Write \pi_{\eta}^{Y} for the Y -marginal, so that \pi_{\eta}^{Y}(\mathrm{d}y)\propto e^{-U_{\eta}(y)}\,\mathrm{d}y ; by ( 2.7 ), \pi_{\eta}^{Y}=\mu*\mathcal{N}(0,\eta I) is a Gaussian smoothing of the target. We use superscripts for marginal and conditional laws; in particular,
\pi_{\eta}^{Y\mid X=x}=\mathcal{N}(x,\eta I)\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y}(\mathrm{d}x)\propto\exp\Bigl\{-V(x)-\frac{\|x-y\|^{2}}{2\eta}\Bigr\}\,\mathrm{d}x\,. (2.8)

Gibbs sampling alternates exact draws from the two conditional laws in ( 2.8 ). The scale \eta controls the strength of the quadratic coupling potential. Decreasing \eta makes X and Y more tightly coupled and the conditional law of X given Y more localized and better conditioned, which reduces the cost of conditional sampling. The resulting transitions are also more local, however, and generally require more Gibbs sampling iterations. Thus \eta balances the cost of each iteration against the number of iterations. The convergence and query complexity are studied further in [ 6 , 9 , 15 ] .
R_{h}\coloneqq I-2\,\frac{hh^{\top}}{\|h\|^{2}}\,,\hskip 20.00003ptR_{0}\coloneqq I\,.

x_{t}-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}=(x_{0}-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\cos t+\sqrt{\eta}\,p_{0}\sin t\,.
Algorithm 1 Simulation of the ideal conditional half-turn process
1: Input: state (x,y)
2: Draw \widetilde{X}\sim\pi_{\eta}^{X\mid Y=y} and p_{0}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I) independently.
3: Query \nabla V(\widetilde{X}) .
4: Set x_{0}\leftarrow x .
5: Evolve (x_{t},p_{t}) according to \dot{x}=\sqrt{\eta}\,p\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\dot{p}=-\frac{x-y}{\sqrt{\eta}}-\sqrt{\eta}\,\nabla V(\widetilde{X})\,, (3.8) until t=\pi .
6: During the evolution, generate bounce events at rate \lambda_{\widetilde{X}}(x,p)=\sqrt{\eta}\,\bigl[p^{\top}[\nabla V(x)-\nabla V(\widetilde{X})]\bigr]_{+}\,. (3.9)
7: At each bounce, set p_{t}\leftarrow R_{\nabla V(x_{t})-\nabla V(\widetilde{X})}p_{t} .
8: return x_{\pi}
Proposition 3.1 (Well-posedness and stationarity of the conditional phase space process) .

For every fixed y,\widetilde{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} and initial phase space point (x_{0},p_{0}) , the event-driven dynamics in Algorithm 1 , with the reference point fixed at \widetilde{x} , defines a unique non-explosive, time-homogeneous Markov process. The phase space measure \nu_{\eta,y} is stationary for this process. In particular, the returned position x_{\pi} is well-defined almost surely.
\begin{split}x_{t+u}-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}&=(x_{t}-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\cos u+\sqrt{\eta}\,p_{t}\sin u\,,\\ p_{t+u}&=-\eta^{-1/2}(x_{t}-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\sin u+p_{t}\cos u\,.\end{split}
Fix y,\widetilde{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} . In the notation of ( 3.4 ), the bounce rate ( 3.9 ) reads
\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p)=\sqrt{\eta}\,[p^{\top}h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)]_{+}\,.
The deterministic harmonic flow, namely the solution ( 4.5 ) of ( 3.8 ), and the bounce map are

\displaystyle\Phi_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(x,p) \displaystyle\coloneqq\bigl(c_{y,\widetilde{x}}+(x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\cos t+\sqrt{\eta}\,p\sin t,\;-\eta^{-1/2}(x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}})\sin t+p\cos t\bigr)\,, \displaystyle\mathsf{S}_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p) \displaystyle\coloneqq(x,R_{h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)}p)\,,\hskip 20.00003ptR_{0}\coloneqq I\,.
The bounce map is an involution. Although there is a possible discontinuity at h_{\widetilde{x}}(x)=0 , this creates no ambiguity because the event rate vanishes there.
Let (E_{n})_{n\geq 1} be independent \operatorname{Exp}(1) random variables. Starting from \zeta_{0}\coloneqq(x_{0},p_{0}) at time T_{0}\coloneqq 0 , define recursively

\displaystyle S_{n+1} \displaystyle\coloneqq\inf\Bigl\{u\geq 0:\int_{0}^{u}\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(\Phi_{s}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}))\,\mathrm{d}s\geq E_{n+1}\Bigr\}\,, (A.1) \displaystyle T_{n+1} \displaystyle\coloneqq T_{n}+S_{n+1}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\zeta_{T_{n+1}}\coloneqq\mathsf{S}_{\widetilde{x}}\bigl(\Phi_{S_{n+1}}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}})\bigr)\,, (A.2)
when S_{n+1}<\infty . If the set is empty, set T_{n+1}=S_{n+1}=\infty and stop the recursion. Between jumps, set \zeta_{T_{n}+t}=\Phi_{t}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}) for 0\leq t<S_{n+1} .
To prove non-explosion, define the shifted harmonic energy
H_{y,\widetilde{x}}(x,p)\coloneqq\frac{1}{2}\,\bigl\{\eta^{-1}\,\|x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}\|^{2}+\|p\|^{2}\bigr\}\,.
The flow and each bounce preserve this energy. Hence, with \mathcal{E}\coloneqq H_{y,\widetilde{x}}(x_{0},p_{0}) , every state produced by the recursion satisfies
\|p\|\leq\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}}\,,\hskip 20.00003pt\|x-c_{y,\widetilde{x}}\|\leq\sqrt{2\eta\mathcal{E}}\,.
Because \nabla V is \beta -Lipschitz, \lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(x,p)\leq\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x}) throughout the path, where
\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})\coloneqq\sqrt{\eta}\,\beta\sqrt{2\mathcal{E}}\,\bigl\{\sqrt{2\eta\mathcal{E}}+\|c_{y,\widetilde{x}}-\widetilde{x}\|\bigr\}\,.
Hence,
\int_{0}^{u}\lambda_{\widetilde{x}}(\Phi_{s}^{y,\widetilde{x}}(\zeta_{T_{n}}))\,\mathrm{d}s\leq\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})\,u\,.
If \bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})=0 , the event rate vanishes and there are no jumps. Otherwise, ( A.1 ) implies, for every finite waiting time,
S_{n+1}\geq\frac{E_{n+1}}{\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})}\,.
If the recursion does not terminate, it follows that
T_{n}\geq\frac{\sum_{j=1}^{n}E_{j}}{\bar{\lambda}_{\mathcal{E}}(y,\widetilde{x})}\longrightarrow\infty

almost surely by the strong law of large numbers. Thus, the jump times cannot accumulate, and the recursive construction defines a unique process for all t\geq 0 . Finally, the memoryless property of the exponential clocks gives the time-homogeneous Markov property. This is precisely the integrated hazard construction of Davis [ 12 , Section 2] . ∎
Proposition A.2 (Joint measurability and augmented space half-turn operator) .

The family of conditional half-turn kernels (\mathcal{H}_{y})_{y\in\mathbb{R}^{d}} admits a version, again denoted by \mathcal{H}_{y}(x,\mathrm{d}x^{\prime}) , such that (y,x)\mapsto\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,A) is Borel measurable for every Borel set A\subset\mathbb{R}^{d} . Consequently,
(\mathsf{H}f)(x,y)\coloneqq\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}f(x^{\prime},y)\,\mathcal{H}_{y}(x,\mathrm{d}x^{\prime}) (A.9)
defines a self-adjoint Markov contraction on L^{2}(\pi_{\eta}) .
